title: Justus von Liebig & William Henry Perkin (1803–1873 / 1838–1907) — The Five-Bulb Kaliapparat, the Mauve Attic, the One-Day Alizarin Race, and Coal-Tar Pharma

teenKit.tldr: An 18-year-old trying to cook up artificial malaria medicine in a freezing London attic accidentally produced a hideous black sludge that gave birth to the global synthetic dye and pharmaceutical industries.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Without this messy chemical accident, our clothes, vibrant plastics, and modern prescription medicines would still rely entirely on what nature managed to grow or extract by hand.
keyTakeaways: Justus von Liebig transformed science education by turning a Hessian police barracks into the world's first modern hands-on PhD research lab.
William Henry Perkin attempted a chemically impossible task—turning coal-tar waste into the complex anti-malarial drug quinine—and failed completely.
Instead of getting medicine, Perkin washed his beaker with alcohol, saw a stunning purple shimmer, and accidentally launched the Mauve Decade of fashion and synthetic chemistry.

vocab.meaning: A five-bulb glass device invented by Justus von Liebig that made analyzing the chemical makeup of organic matter fast, safe, and accurate.
A foul-smelling, toxic oily compound derived from industrial coal tar that serves as the base building block for many synthetic dyes and drugs.
A rare and intensely bitter natural medicine extracted from tree bark that was historically the only known defense against malaria.
A confident attempt to build a complex molecule using a chemical equation that math and atomic reality simply do not allow.

quiz.question: What was William Henry Perkin originally trying to create in his freezing London attic?
quiz.explanation: Perkin was attempting to artificially synthesize quinine, the vital anti-malarial drug, using coal-tar derivatives.

quiz.question: What did Perkin find in his beaker after reacting aniline with a harsh oxidizer?
options: Bright purple liquid ready for shirts
quiz.explanation: The initial reaction produced a hopeless, jet-black sludge that initially looked like a total chemical failure.

quiz.question: How did Justus von Liebig fundamentally change scientific research in the 19th century?
options: He proved that coal tar could be turned into medicine.
He invented the first mechanized clothing loom.
He created the modern university lab where students learned by doing experiments.
He discovered how to cure malaria without tree bark.
quiz.explanation: Liebig revolutionized chemistry education by moving students out of lecture halls and into hands-on research laboratories.
